task: SCS-003 Booking MVP (Issue #57, ADR-0014): the third Class A Business System of the Application Factory at Level 0. Owns tenant-scoped Resources, their Availability Windows and Reservations behind the same enforcement chain as SCS-001/SCS-002, reuses IS-001 (tenant context), IS-003 (decision), IS-005 (exactly-once commands) and the audit semantics, and proves the no-double-booking invariant atomically under concurrency. Live operations: seven — create and read one owned Resource, declare and list its Availability Windows, create, read and cancel one Reservation.

invariants: B-001 every Resource, Availability Window and Reservation has exactly one data owner and belongs to exactly one Tenant
B-002 a subject of Tenant A never reaches Booking data of Tenant B, including by changing an identifier or a caller-supplied tenant_id
B-003 a request with an IS-003 DENY never reaches the owned-data operation
B-004 an authorization dependency failure or a malformed/non-authoritative dependency answer fails closed to DENY
B-005 the effective tenant comes from IS-001; this component creates no second tenant-context mechanism
B-006 the public surface provides no access path that bypasses the Booking enforcement boundary
B-007 security-sensitive refusals are auditable and observable with request/correlation and actor/tenant context where applicable
B-008 the internals of this component are not a consumer contract: a consumer receives the published client and values only

B-009 every interval is half-open [start_at, end_at) with start_at < end_at; API input must be timezone-aware (naive timestamps are refused), persistence and comparison are in UTC, and adjacent intervals never overlap
B-010 an Availability Window is an explicit allowed interval of one Resource of the same Tenant — not a slot, not occupancy; windows may overlap each other freely

B-011 a Reservation is created only when the Resource exists in the Tenant, is ACTIVE, the interval is valid, lies entirely inside one Availability Window, and no ACTIVE Reservation of the Resource overlaps it; check and insert are one atomic step inside the Resource's critical section, so no interleaving yields two ACTIVE overlapping Reservations
B-012 the Reservation lifecycle is exactly ACTIVE → CANCELLED: cancellation preserves the record, no CANCELLED → ACTIVE move, no repeated cancel, no delete; a cancelled interval is bookable again

B-013 the booker is the opaque booker_identity_id of the verified subject — never supplied by the caller; only the booker cancels its Reservation (booker_mismatch otherwise, even inside the same Tenant)
B-014 Booking depends on neither Commerce nor Learning and modifies neither; no pricing, payment, capacity, recurrence, waitlist, notification or calendar concept exists

resource_model.note: tenant_id and owner_component are store facts of each record and are not published in the views. created_by and booker_identity_id are opaque references to the verified identity — Identity owns the profile, Booking stores and never interprets the reference. Timestamps are served as ISO 8601 with the explicit +00:00 offset.

operations.purpose: create one owned Resource in the effective tenant of the verified identity; status defaults to ACTIVE and may be declared INACTIVE
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded result without a second effect, and a changed binding (payload, identity, tenant, operation, target) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The payload fingerprint is computed over the UTC-normalized interval, so two spellings of the same instant are the same command. The command has no pre-existing target: the IS-005 resource binding is empty, and the tenant binding is the effective tenant of the chain.

operations.purpose: serve one owned Resource after the enforcement chain allowed the access
operations.idempotency_note: A read changes no state beyond the append-only audit journal.

operations.purpose: declare one Availability Window [start_at, end_at) of an existing Resource of the effective tenant; windows are explicit allowed intervals, not slots or occupancy
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded result without a second effect, and a changed binding (payload, identity, tenant, operation, target) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The payload fingerprint is computed over the UTC-normalized interval, so two spellings of the same instant are the same command. The IS-005 resource binding is the Resource.

operations.purpose: serve the Availability Windows of one owned Resource in ascending start_at order
operations.idempotency_note: A read changes no state beyond the append-only audit journal.

operations.purpose: reserve one half-open interval [start_at, end_at) of an ACTIVE Resource of the effective tenant for the verified subject; the five creation conditions (Resource exists in the Tenant, Resource ACTIVE, valid aware interval, fully inside one Availability Window, no ACTIVE overlap) are checked and the record inserted atomically inside the Resource's critical section
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded result without a second effect, and a changed binding (payload, identity, tenant, operation, target) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The payload fingerprint is computed over the UTC-normalized interval, so two spellings of the same instant are the same command. The IS-005 resource binding is the Resource; a refused reservation (409) records no idempotency result, so the same key may retry after the interval frees.

operations.purpose: serve one owned Reservation (ACTIVE or CANCELLED) after the enforcement chain allowed the access
operations.idempotency_note: A read changes no state beyond the append-only audit journal.

operations.purpose: move one ACTIVE Reservation of the verified subject to CANCELLED; the record is preserved, its interval becomes bookable again; a second cancel is invalid_state_transition and another booker of the same Tenant is booker_mismatch
operations.idempotency_note: State-changing command guarded by IS-005: the Idempotency-Key header is mandatory, an exact replay returns the recorded result without a second effect, and a changed binding (payload, identity, tenant, operation, target) is refused as IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The payload fingerprint is computed over the UTC-normalized interval, so two spellings of the same instant are the same command. The command carries no body; the IS-005 resource binding is the Reservation.

enforcement_model.passed_through_denials: the published deny reasons of IS-003, unchanged
enforcement_model.nonauthoritative_answers: an answer outside the published decision model of IS-003 — including an ALLOW with a reason other than permitted and a DENY with an unknown reason — fails closed as authorization_unavailable

time_semantics.input: ISO 8601 with an explicit offset or Z; a naive timestamp is validation_error
time_semantics.storage_and_comparison: UTC; two spellings of one instant are the same instant for conflict, containment and idempotency
time_semantics.containment: a Reservation must lie entirely within one Availability Window (bounds inclusive)

enforcement_model.concurrency: the no-double-booking decision and the insert run inside the exclusive critical section of the target Resource (BookingStore.resource_section); reads never enter it; under a race with different Idempotency-Keys exactly one contender is served and the other receives reservation_conflict

refusal_semantics.principle: a refusal is data with a stable machine-readable code and reason, audited with request_id and correlation_id; nothing about this surface can be mistaken for a served record

error.message: the stable message of the code

shape.request_id: the request_id the refusal was audited with
shape.correlation_id: the correlation_id the refusal was audited with

AUTHORIZATION_DENIED.reasons: tenant_mismatch, tenant_unknown, platform_ownership_mismatch, resource_tenant_unknown, resource_tenant_mismatch, tenant_not_active, tenant_suspended, tenant_deletion_requested, tenant_deleted, permission_not_granted, authority_unavailable, missing_tenant_context, owner_mismatch, booker_mismatch

INVALID_REQUEST.message: Request does not match the published contract.
INVALID_REQUEST.note: defence in depth: the schema handler refuses a request the published contract cannot read (e.g. a command body with a missing field, a wrong type or a declared-unknown field such as booker_identity_id) before any handler runs; the stable reason is malformed_request

VALIDATION_ERROR.note: the payload is readable but breaks a domain rule of the command: blank name, unknown status, a naive (offset-less) or unparsable timestamp, or start_at >= end_at once both bounds are compared in UTC; refused before any decision is asked

RESOURCE_INACTIVE.message: Resource is inactive and accepts no new reservations.

OUTSIDE_AVAILABILITY.message: Requested interval is not within an availability window.
OUTSIDE_AVAILABILITY.note: availability_not_found — the Resource has no Availability Window at all; outside_availability — windows exist but none contains [start_at, end_at) entirely (an interval bridging two windows is contained in neither)

RESERVATION_CONFLICT.message: Requested interval conflicts with an active reservation.
RESERVATION_CONFLICT.note: an ACTIVE Reservation of the same Resource overlaps [start_at, end_at) on the half-open rule (adjacent intervals never conflict); decided atomically inside the Resource's critical section, so under concurrency exactly one of two contenders is served

INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION.message: Operation is not valid for the current state.

IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REQUIRED.message: An Idempotency-Key header is required for this operation.

IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.message: The Idempotency-Key was already used with a different request.

envelope.note: The HTTP status selects the code; the stable internal reason is preserved in error.details.reason; request_id and correlation_id match the audit record of the refusal.

refused.403: tenant_mismatch, tenant_unknown, platform_ownership_mismatch, resource_tenant_unknown, resource_tenant_mismatch, tenant_not_active, tenant_suspended, tenant_deletion_requested, tenant_deleted, permission_not_granted, authority_unavailable, missing_tenant_context, owner_mismatch, booker_mismatch
refused.409: resource_inactive, availability_not_found, outside_availability, reservation_conflict, invalid_state_transition, idempotency_conflict

refusal_semantics.served: HTTP 200/201 with the published representation — resource, availability window(s) or reservation — produced only by the owned-data operation at the end of the enforcement chain

consumer_surface.transport: booking_service.transport.open_channel + booking_service.transport.call_contract — the published HTTP contract executed in process over an opaque channel handle (ARCHITECTURE.md §1.1 interaction mode API, Level 0)
errors: booking_service.errors.AccessRefused — the access did not happen; the reason is one of the published refusal reasons (400/401/403/404/409/422/503), carried in error.details.reason, with the request_id/correlation_id of the refusal
booking_service.errors.ContractViolation — the contract transport failed or answered outside its published shape (including any non-envelope shape); a consumer must fail closed
guarantees: values only: no booking store, audit journal, engine reference or deployment is reachable through the published surface
the published client holds no callable and no credential: its state is one channel handle, so walking the client and its class reaches neither the component's ASGI application nor its internals
the subject credential is supplied per access and verified by IS-001 inside the IS-003 decision: a consumer cannot assert who the subject or the booker is
the ASGI application is never handed out: it stays behind the provider-side channel table, and a channel is revoked when the consumer drops the client
importing the published module binds no reference to booking_service.transport — its namespace holds no module object, no channel table and no transport type
an unknown or revoked channel handle raises ContractViolation, so there is no permissive fallback and a handle cannot be guessed
every access runs through the same routing, enforcement chain and audit code that serves an HTTP request
there is no resource or reservation listing, search, calendar view, bulk export, pagination or raw-store operation: the seven published operations are the only access paths, and all are enforced
the state-changing commands own no second idempotency mechanism: each is delivered to the IS-005 guard, which decides between executing, replaying and refusing a conflict
composition_root_only: the contract application itself (the ASGI application) — a consumer component must not own or re-export it
the contract channel table booking_service.transport._CHANNELS — a handle-to-application mapping owned by the component
consumer_surface.note: The deployment object is composition-internal: it assembles engine, store and contract application for the composition root and for this component's own tests and is never handed to a consumer. This component composes no other component and publishes no module-level demo application: a demo of a data owner needs a composed Platform Instance with a live decision dependency, and composing one is the job of a composition root.

consumes.mechanism: contract client over the published API of authorization, executed in process at Level 0
consumes.credential_source: deployment secret resolved by the composition root: the service identity of this component
consumes.note: The access decision is read per access and never cached. The resource's owning Tenant stated in the question comes from this component's own store — or, for the resource-create command whose target does not exist yet, from the effective tenant of the verified identity — never from a caller claim (LAW-16a).
consumes.dependency_isolation: No module of booking imports authorization_service, identity_service, tenant_authority, commerce_service or learning_service: the published client is adapted at the composition boundary and only values owned by this component reach the enforcement logic (ARCHITECTURE.md 1.1, 6.1, LAW-04).

consumes.mechanism: contract client over the published API of identity, executed in process at Level 0
consumes.credential_source: the subject credential presented on the published surface; the adapter adds nothing
consumes.note: Consumed by exactly one command — resource create — whose target does not exist yet, so the resource Tenant of its authorization question can only be the effective tenant of the verified identity (the chain Identity -> effective tenant -> Authorization -> Booking ownership boundary). Every other operation states the Tenant of the existing Resource or Reservation from the store. No second identity or tenant mechanism exists: the port carries the answer of IS-001 and nothing else.

events.note: SCS-003 publishes no inter-component events, sends no notifications and does not simulate a broker. The access audit journal is owned data, not a public event contract.

data_export_cdc.note: No CDC, calendar feed or bulk export stream is implemented in this slice. A bulk path would be a bypass risk for the enforcement boundary and is deliberately out of this slice.

ui.note: Class A Business System / SCS; UI is out of this Level 0 slice. Every published operation is proven at the API boundary.

platform_id.description: Identifier of the Platform Instance this data owner serves.

datasets.name: resources
datasets.note: Every Resource has exactly one data owner and belongs to exactly one Tenant; status is ACTIVE or INACTIVE; the Tenant comes from the verified identity through the published chain, never from a caller claim. Domain-agnostic: no Commerce or Learning internals, no price, no capacity.

datasets.name: availability_windows
datasets.note: Every Availability Window belongs to exactly one Resource of the same Tenant; a half-open UTC interval declaring when the Resource may be reserved. Windows are permission, not occupancy: they are not consumed by Reservations and may overlap each other.

datasets.name: reservations
datasets.note: Every Reservation belongs to exactly one Resource of the same Tenant and to one opaque booker_identity_id; a half-open UTC interval with status ACTIVE or CANCELLED. Only ACTIVE Reservations occupy time. Cancelled records are preserved history; no delete exists.

datasets.name: access_audit
datasets.note: Append-only journal of every access attempt — served or refused — with request/correlation and actor/tenant context where known, including IS-005 replays and conflicts.

notes: This component owns no identity, no permission grant, no tenant registry and no tenant state: those belong to identity, authorization and tenant_authority and are read through their published contracts.

The Resource → Availability Window / Reservation parentage is registered, never declared by a caller: the store refuses orphan and cross-tenant children, duplicate identifiers, naive or non-UTC bounds and invalid intervals at registration.

The per-Resource critical section is a domain lock of the Level 0 in-memory store; a persistent store must reproduce the same atomicity (row lock or serializable transaction) — the invariant, not the mechanism, is the contract.

audit.journal: internal append-only journal owned by booking
audit.refusal_audit_scope: every refusal of the published contract, including a request rejected by the contract schema before any handler runs, a domain refusal (reservation_conflict, outside_availability, resource_inactive, invalid_state_transition, booker_mismatch) and a refusal produced because the decision dependency did not answer; the record carries request_id and correlation_id of the caller
audit.note: Audit is owned data, not a public event contract, and is not readable through the published surface.

observability.saga_id: absent — this component runs no inter-component sagas

authn.note: The subject credential presented on the public surface is verified by IS-001 inside the IS-003 decision; this component verifies no credential itself. When asking IS-003, this component authenticates with its own service identity (demo: authz-svc-token-booking).

authz.note: ALLOW from IS-003 is not direct data access: the data owner remains the final enforcement boundary (ARCHITECTURE.md §6.2). A decision that cannot be obtained is a denial. The seven operations each carry their own grant — no role or policy logic exists inside Booking. Cancellation additionally requires the verified subject to be the booker of the Reservation (booker_mismatch), checked by the data owner after the grant. The resource-create command has no pre-existing target, so its authorization question names the effective tenant of the verified identity resolved through IS-001; no second identity, tenant, authorization or idempotency mechanism is introduced.

compatibility_policy.reason_codes: adding a refusal reason is a minor change; removing or redefining one is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.enforcement_chain: reordering or removing a step is a breaking change: the order is part of the published behaviour
compatibility_policy.resource_model: adding a field to a published representation is a minor change; changing the published fields of Resource, Availability Window or Reservation is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.time_semantics: the half-open interval rule, the aware-input/UTC-storage rule and the containment rule are part of the published behaviour; changing any of them is a breaking change
compatibility_policy.lifecycle: the Reservation lifecycle is exactly ACTIVE → CANCELLED and the Resource status vocabulary is exactly ACTIVE/INACTIVE; adding states or transitions is a new architectural decision, not a silent change
compatibility_policy.error_envelope: the approved envelope shape is part of the contract; changing error/code/message/details/request_id/correlation_id is a breaking change

dependencies.direction: booking -> idempotency (exactly-once delivery of the state-changing commands)
dependencies.note: SCS-003 implements no second idempotency mechanism: every state-changing command identity (operation, UTC-normalized payload fingerprint) is delivered to IS-005, which decides between executing, replaying and refusing a conflict.

dependencies.direction: booking -> identity (tenant context of the verified subject for the resource-create command without a target)
dependencies.note: Consumed only because the resource-create command has no pre-existing resource whose Tenant the store could state. The effective tenant still comes from IS-001 and from nowhere else; a caller-supplied tenant_id remains a cross-check (LAW-16a).
